MFA No.202070/2017 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - II, Yadgiri, (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.138/2016 while MFA No.201563/2017 is filed by the North Eastern Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Limited ('Corporation' for short) challenging the liability fastened on it as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.138/2016 vide judgment and award dated 28.03.2017.

sentences.text: 2. The appellants in MFA No.202070/2017 and respondent Nos.1 to 5 in MFA No.201563/2017 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'claimants'.
The respondent in MFA No.202070/2017, who is the appellant in MFA No.201563/2017 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'insurer' / 'Corporation' of the bus involved in the accident.

The claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased Sri Basavaraj who was killed in a road traffic accident that happened when he along with another was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32- EN-4876 on 24.05.2016 at 2.30 p.m. on Hurusgundi-Kollur main road and when they approached near Kanagnahali cross, a bus belonging to the Corporation bearing No.KA- 33-F-0032 (henceforth referred to as 'the offending vehicle') dashed against the said motorcycle.

The claimants claimed that the deceased was aged 35 years old at the time of the accident and was working as a labourer and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month which he used to contribute to the family.
Therefore, the claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the Corporation.
4. The Corporation contested the claim petition denying that the accident was due to the negligence of its driver.
It also denied the income, nature of work and age NC: 2023:KHC-K:1270 of the deceased Basavaraj at the time of the accident.

It alleged that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and therefore, it was not liable to pay any compensation.
5.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked documents as Exs.P1 to P6.
The Corporation examined its driver as RW.1 but did not mark any documentary evidence.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In so far as the claim for compensation is concerned, it held that the age of the deceased was between 36 to 40 years as per the ration card - Ex.P6.

It held that the notional income of the deceased was a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month and since the deceased left behind five dependants, it deducted 1/4th of the income NC:

7. Being aggrieved by the above, separate appeals are filed by the claimants as well as the Corporation.

8. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal was not justified in considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month while in similar circumstances, this Court has NC: 2023:KHC-K:1270 considered Rs.8,750/- per month as notional income of persons who died in road traffic accidents that happened in 2016.

He also claimed that the Tribunal did not consider the loss of future prospects as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and others [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and others [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submitted that the Tribunal failed to award adequate compensation towards loss of filial consortium to each of the claimants.

9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Corporation contended that two vehicles were involved in the accident in a head on collision and it was the deceased who was negligent and responsible for the accident.
Therefore, he contends that the Tribunal must not have fastened liability on the Corporation to pay the compensation.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the Corporation.
Though the Corporation claimed that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased, it did not produce any material evidence in that regard.
The evidence of RW.1 was not trustworthy as he was an employee of the Corporation, who was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to prove that the deceased was responsible for the accident, the contention of the learned counsel for the Corporation that the Dodda Maremma And Ors vs The Divisional Controller on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21235785/
5 deceased was negligent and caused the accident cannot be accepted and therefore, the appeal filed by the Corporation does not merit consideration.
